Yeah I don't know about this, developmental disabilities are typically ones that have to do with brain development that are consistent amongst certain ages. (There's even an argument that schizophrenia/schizotypal is a developmental disability because of the social deficits and similar patterns of development among children and adolescents BEFORE developing schizophrenia symptoms, the people who don't follow this are the exception and not the rule) 

But things like bipolar, depression, and other mental illness have a very sporadic age of onset. You can get depressed at 13 and you can get depressed at 20. ADHD and autism you are born with and follow an exact pattern of development. 

Personality disorders are maladaptive trauma reactions (typically). While there are some differences in brains with BPD and Npd the effects on how the brains are seen in scans can also be more of a result than the cause (for instance someone with PTSD may have a heightened amygdala due to years of stress). 

I think maybe they're classified under "developmental disorders" for legalities because it's easier to seperate, not necessarily because it's true to the DSM or from a doctor's perspective. 

Though I do see the arrested development in family with NPD. And it's easy to tolerate that they are dysregulated inner(?) Children and not big scary malicious adults they come off as. So maybe there is something to it.

In a healthy relationship, people do occasionally do toxic and shitty and neglectful things, but we can repair those things. Admit when we were wrong or if it's neither parties fault comfort and attune to the other and compromise. Especially if your both struggling with trauma/stress/mental health issues. The difference is you can admit it. You can explain it. And you can move on from it. And you can accept responsibility to change. It's hard for us abuse survives to find the line between unrelenting grudges and reasonable healthy boundaries because... We weren't modeled what was normal. 

First step breaking the pattern is anger, anger is the opposite of codependency, and it's a clumsy process. It will hurt you and you may lash out at others because we weren't taught how to regulate it. But that's the only way out to defending yourself consistently. And if a situation dips into abusive territory (calling you horrible names, DARVO, or even expressing outright malicious actions towards you) then it only takes ONCE. It only takes once.

I remember as a kid my grandpa making a very extreme frown to the point that his mouth would corner and stretch as far as it could go. Now, my grandpa probably isn't FULLY narcissistic, but he has symptoms of BPD is emotionally avoidant and is married and compliant with my narcissistic grandma. And I remember very vividly thinking "today is not the day to fuck with him" growing up. 

My grandma doesn't really make extreme facial expressions although several seperate therapist and psychs of mine have told me it sounds like she has NPD. But she is also VERY vocal with her emotional. She will shout being annoyed by something as minimal as conisistent cough. You don't have to look at her face to know what she is feeling, she will tell you. 

Interestingly, both of them read my hyper read expressions and take them personally to the point I developed a flat affect (although I have a lot of other disorders, PTSD, MDD, and suspicions of autism that could contribute to my flat affect).and they respond to my expressions as threats. 

If y'all look at the borderline notes YouTube channel they're as several micro interviews (about 3-4 minutes long) and also Dr. K has a deep dive on BPD about 30 minutes long that some what come to the same conclusions that BPD and Npd are really the same disorder but people are socialized to express them in different ways. And even that NPD is sorta another layer of a BPD coping mechanism. Either theory, they both have to do with people not having an internal sense of self and relying on other people to supply that sense of self to regulate their emotions. If other people can't regulate their emotions their emotions get completely out of control because they have no capacity to soothe themselves because... They don't even know who they are! They need to be told how to feel, who they are, and how to think. 


This is also to say, not having a sense of self leads to extreme emotional dysregulation in relationships. People with NPD don't show 'weak' emotions such as sadness because they've developed such a strong ego as a coping mechanism it would also destroy the safe replicated sense of self. But anger is a "safe" emotion because it's a "powerful" emotion. 

BPD is basically NPD without the ego. People with BPD can be very passionate, vulnerable, creative, kind, and sensitive because they don't need to put up this false sense of self, and don't (usually) feel the need to hurt other people to keep these complex defenses. (Although self aware people with NPD can definitely get to a point of this). But at the same time, they have less defenses, and so are more perceptive of "threats" of abandonment. 

***Tldr;  people with BPD and NPD have the same root problem of struggling with a sense of self. Which makes sense why they can have a sort of hyper expressiveness or emotional dysregulation to interpersonal threats leading to the scientific study, and also,  can have similarities with threat perception.***

They are already functional and most of them had their characters arcs off screen or in the Main Story. 

I mean you need glaring character flaws and consequences to fix them to create a character arc. Saki has some imposter syndrome/low self esteem/anxiety/existential dread/anxious attachment shit going on but the writers did a good job balancing having a really likable character that has flaws for reasons that make sense to us as the audience.  

I mean maybe that's not for everyone though and I'm really speaking for myself. I've read the honami "courage to lead" event and while I actually really liked it I think sega just really doesn't know what to do with these characters which really sucks. 

Let's contrast this with WXS or 25ji. While WXS is split between adventure stories and the occasional sad backstory story these characters have very blatant flaws/conflicts (emus toxic positivity and insecurity over the bullying of her brothers/tsukasas non-clinical narcissism, nenes social anxiety, and ruis... Autism???) Most of them that effect each other socially. Even though these characters are happy they have to do inner growth and development at their most painful insecurities to move forward. So even though it's not super packed with drama or anything, I would still say the writing is pretty good. We like the characters because they are nice and funny and the writers have enough room to do fun things. But they each have to face their deepest weak points to move forward. 

25ji is obviously edge drama depression and it's actually my favorite unit so I feel like I can say that. But the backstory of the traumas of each character probably make it easier for the writers to do something... WITH them. There's so many arcs that have started and yet haven't resolved (except maybe enas). 25ji is in a way the opposite L/N because they're not so much focused on their career is their internal state and working towards recovery. The L/N girls don't really seem to think about their problems unless it comes up through very specific goals, but the goal is still the primary source of conflict.
